dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh, you're here! I was just starting to wonder if I should send you clearer instructions...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: But then I thought, if I make my hints too obvious, it might get in the way of your travel plans...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: And then, just as I was pacing back and forth, agonizing over what I was going to do... you turned up here anyway! So, it looks like everything worked out fine!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Nicole! You're so full of energy today! And... words... you're so full of words...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I'll take that as a compliment! Alright then, are you ready to check out my next room?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the—!? Paimon almost had a heart attack, being sucked in by a painting like that! ...Wait a sec, this place looks familiar... Oh, it's the table where the mages hold their tea parties!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It all started the first time Alice invited me for tea...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: On that day, I didn't attend in person — mostly because, back then, I still hadn't decided whether I really wanted to join the Hexenzirkel or not.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Alice was the only one there who knew my true identity. She warned me not to say a word, or let anyone else discover who I was. I was only supposed to observe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...And then what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Well... Then, I concluded that she was punishing me for my hesitation to join.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Everyone was talking about such interesting things. How could I not chime in?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: And of course, when you're in the middle of a conversation, and someone throws out a question you know the answer to, how are you supposed to keep your mouth shut?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Which brings us to the bet between Barbeloth and Alice, Rhinedottir's forbidden creations, Ivanovna's political machinations...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It was like a series of exquisitely acted plays, distilled within the confines of a teacup. Their words alone were enough to ignite my instinct to lay the truth bare before them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you piped up inside their heads?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Of course not! Even though I felt like my head was going to explode, I still made sure to hold it all in. I'm a responsible angel, after all — and I'm well aware of the difference between "what I want to say" and "what I'm allowed to say."

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: So I had a private little word with Alice inside her head — just me and her — and I agreed to join the Hexenzirkel, right there and then.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: She was quite happy about my decision, but as for the talking inside her head... Well, she claims that over the next few days, she had such a headache that she had to visit a doctor in Liyue to get some relief. But she can hardly blame me for that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that an Irminsul tree?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh, this painting here? You're clearly no strangers to the white trees... but did you know that the first angel's betrayal happened beneath one of their very boughs?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Well then, I guess it's finally time for me to tell you a tale of romance and horror. Let me just think how best to protect the identity of those involved... Alright, got it!

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: A long, long time ago, there was once a traveler who wandered among the stars. They were nothing like you... but that's not important right now.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: One day, he traveled to a silver tree to visit the Princess of the Morning Star. Before long, he started asking her about her kingdom's most forbidden secrets.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: His words puzzled the princess. How could he possibly know of all these things forbidden by the gods?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: The young man revealed his origins and showed the princess things she had never seen before — of free will and love, both noble and spiritual.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: His words awakened her sense of self, hitherto shackled by the gods. Her heart soared, carrying her beyond limits she had never crossed before...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: The Princess of the Morning Star confided the kingdom's secrets to the youth, and between them, love grew and blossomed — along with a determination to defy the gods.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is just a cookie-cutter love story! You said there'd be horror...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Don't worry, Paimon, the horror's about to begin. They yearned to help the people live lives of unfettered freedom, but the gods could not forgive their betrayal.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: They sent down thunder and fury, destroying the lovers' home. And when the great war subsided, the power and the wisdom of the princess were lost, never to return...

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Even her closest friends were cursed...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Uhhh, yeah... That ending was pretty scary, after all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But didn't you say you were going to tell us about the first angel? And, and... you're not saying this story's actually true, are you...?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: It sure is, and that's the scariest part.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Well then, I guess it's finally time for me to tell you a tale of romance and horror.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Let me just think how best to protect the identity of those involved...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, this is Simulanka! Uhm... but why are there light novels from Yae Publishing House all over the floor?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Well, on the subject of my literary enlightenment, my greatest inspiration of all... is none other than Lady Anya herself.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: She was the last to join the Hexenzirkel, and yet the first to leave...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I loved all of her stories. Whether it was just an idea or a fully fleshed-out manuscript, Anya was always so skilled at making her readers gasp with joy.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hexenzirkel discussions rarely stray far from magic, and it's my belief that Anya possessed a unique magic of her own. She could weave love and compassion into words and stories that would touch the hearts of others.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I asked her for tips on how to write compelling tales. She taught me a lot of tricks and techniques, but in the end, my biggest enemy has always been myself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Too lazy to put pen to paper?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Haha! That's one way of putting it. Communicating through thought is so much more convenient. I guess even angels can succumb to laziness.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: However, recently I've resolved to make an effort, even if it's just to spare myself reproaches from a certain old Seelie friend of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Does that mean we're finally gonna get to read something you've written?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Who said anything about writing? I'm talking about buying popular works from the last few centuries to flip through in my spare time.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Haha! That's one way of putting it.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Communicating through thought is so much more convenient.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I guess even angels can succumb to laziness.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: These paintings all remind me of places that hold great significance in my heart. And now, the studio has been fully restored.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Alright, go ahead and claim our reward. What? Don't look at me like that! Of course, this reward is "ours."

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: You're not going to leave this chest unopened, are you? I can't let you leave if you do. Besides, after telling you so many stories, don't I deserve a reward of my own?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ahem... You still haven't taken everything!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Come to think of it... this mage's lodge holds a special significance for me, too. A painting within a house, a house within a painting... worlds within worlds. Fascinating, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this Nicole's studio? Why is it just a bunch of empty frames on white walls...? Let's take a closer look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How about we go look at the other frames? Paimon's starting to feel like she needs some relief, too...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ahem... You still haven't taken everything!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: A happy story all wrapped up! See you next time.
